activities.caption: pair the side chain with its amino acid
activities.name: psaSideMatch

config.prompt: Five side chains, five identities — pair them:

pairs.left: a single hydrogen atom — the smallest possible side chain
a tip ending in a negative electric charge
a tip ending in a positive electric charge
a sulfur-bearing tip that clamps onto another of its own kind

config.why: The side chain (R group) is each letter's identity: glycine minimal, leucine oily, aspartate and lysine oppositely charged, cysteine the clamp that can later staple the fold shut.

activities.anchor: The twenty side chains form a small chemistry set
activities.caption: file the twenty letters into families
activities.name: psaFamilyBuckets

config.prompt: File each side chain into its family:

items.label: the kind that gets buried in the fold's greasy interior

config.why: Hydrophobic side chains hide from water and pack inside; polar uncharged ones are water-friendly without a charge; charged ones face out — or pair up in salt bridges. Glycine, proline and cysteine are the specialists outside these families.

activities.anchor: How do blocks become a chain?
activities.caption: fill the blanks — how blocks become a chain
activities.name: psaBondCloze

config.text: The %%0%% end of one amino acid links to the acid end of the next; forming this peptide bond squeezes out a molecule of %%1%%, so the reaction is called a %%2%%. Sequences are always written N to C — and the N stands for %%3%%.
config.hint: One end carries a free amino group; think of what squirts from the joint when two bricks click together.

activities.anchor: Sizes vary. Two joined amino acids are a
activities.caption: call the magnitude — insulin's length
activities.name: psaInsulinEstimate

config.prompt: Proteins run from dozens to thousands of blocks. Insulin, the small hormone that has been sequenced and injected for a century — roughly how many amino acids long is it?
config.why: Insulin is 51 amino acids long; titin, among the largest, is some 34,000 — three orders of magnitude of chain in one cell.
config.context: Two joined amino acids are a dipeptide; a short chain an oligopeptide; a protein dozens to thousands.

activities.anchor: One is feeble; thousands grip firmly
activities.caption: true or false — helices, sheets and staples
activities.name: psaSecondaryJudge

statements.s: Hair keratin is largely alpha helices — which is why wet hair stretches and re-forms as it dries.
statements.why: The backbone hydrogen bonds slip when wet, then grip again on drying.

statements.s: Silk is strong along the strands because it is largely beta sheets.
statements.why: Extended stretches lie side by side and grip across, like zipper teeth closing in a line.

statements.s: Perm solution reshapes hair by breaking the peptide bonds of the backbone.
statements.why: It breaks the disulfide staples — the permanent chemical staples cysteine pairs add to the fold.

statements.s: Quaternary structure means one long chain folded into four lobes.
statements.why: It is separate chains teaming up — haemoglobin is four chains, two of one kind, two of another.

config.prompt: Anfinsen's ribonuclease, 1960s — drag the divider from denatured to refolded:

before.label: denatured
before.text: Ribonuclease stripped of its working shape by the disrupter — an inactive tangle, like the egg white in the pan.

after.label: refolded
after.text: Disrupter removed, nothing re-added: the chain settles back into its native structure — fully active.

config.why: The sequence alone, in the right environment, carries the instructions for the final shape — the licence for all structure prediction.

activities.anchor: stack into fibres, and deform the red blood cell
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the sickle-cell answer
activities.name: psaSickleSpot

config.prompt: This exam answer on sickle-cell anaemia contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Haemoglobin's beta chain is 146 amino acids long.
At position 6, glutamate — charged and outward-facing — is replaced by valine, an oily residue.
The swap puts an oily patch on the protein's surface.
Haemoglobins stick together there, stack into fibres, and deform the red blood cell.
The changed gene persists in malarial regions because one copy makes malaria MORE likely, balancing harm against benefit.
One letter out of 146 — the entire disease.
config.correction: One copy of the changed gene PROTECTS against malaria — selection balances the harm against that benefit.
config.why: The balance runs the other way: the harm (sickle disease) is the price the population pays for the benefit (malaria resistance carried by one copy).

config.root: A new chain is emerging from the ribosome into the crowded cytoplasm — 20–40 per cent of the volume is other macromolecules, and the chain's exposed oily patches are danger zones.

start.text: Those oily patches could stick to the wrong neighbour. What does the cell's support system do?

choices.label: Bind chaperones to the oily regions
choices.feedback: Hsp70 and chaperonin family members grip and shield the patches.

choices.label: Leave the chain to fold unaided in the crowd
choices.feedback: A few chains manage; many stick to the wrong surface.

choices.label: Send the fresh chain straight to the proteasome
choices.feedback: Premature — the shredder is for hopeless cases, not new arrivals.

shield.text: The chain is sheltered. How does it get its fair chance to fold?

choices.label: Hold it steady while it folds in place
choices.feedback: Shielded from wrong neighbours, it folds in the open.

choices.label: Enclose it in a barrel-shaped room
choices.feedback: Chaperonins give it a private room to fold undisturbed.

risk.text: The chain has stuck to a neighbour and folded badly. Now what?

choices.label: Spend ATP to pull the trapped chain out
choices.feedback: Some chaperones burn the cell's energy currency to rescue trapped chains.

choices.label: Escort it to the proteasome
choices.feedback: Hopeless case — the shredder digests it.

barrel.text: Inside the barrel it folds undisturbed — the managed version of the funnel.

rescue.text: Rescued — the chain gets another fair chance at its native fold.

shred.text: Digested and recycled. Folding is a managed process, not chemistry alone.

earlyshred.text: A fresh chain destroyed before it ever had a chance — triage has an order.

config.why: Chaperones shield oily patches, hold or enclose chains, spend ATP on rescues, and escort hopeless cases to the proteasome — which is why they are called heat-shock proteins: their production surges when heat shakes proteins loose.
